stack.title: Jesus's brothers and sisters
stack.hook: The Bible says Jesus had brothers and sisters. So who were they?

cards.head: The Bible says Jesus had brothers and sisters.
cards.body: So who were they? The Gospels explicitly mention Jesus's brothers James, Joseph, Judas and Simon and say he had sisters. What Christians have debated for centuries is what exactly "brothers and sisters" means.

cr.line: James the Just (Novgorod, 16 c.).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: MARK ACTUALLY NAMES THEM
cards.body: In Mark 6, people in Jesus's hometown identify him as Mary's son and name four brothers. His sisters are mentioned too, although their names aren't given.

cr.line: Andrea Mantegna (workshop) Holy Family.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: AT FIRST, HIS FAMILY DIDN'T SEEM CONVINCED
cards.body: The Gospels contain surprisingly tense moments involving Jesus's family. John even states that at one point his brothers did not believe in him.

cards.head: THEN SOMETHING CHANGED
cards.body: After Jesus's death, his brother James emerges as one of the most important leaders of the Jerusalem Christian community. Paul specifically describes meeting "James, the Lord's brother."

cards.head: WERE THEY MARY'S OTHER CHILDREN?
cards.body: Many Protestants interpret the passages straightforwardly as younger children of Mary and Joseph. That would make them Jesus's biological half-siblings.

cr.line: On Nazareth hill (1915) (14761720336).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: CATHOLICS AND ORTHODOX CHRISTIANS INTERPRET IT DIFFERENTLY
cards.body: Catholic tradition generally understands them as close relatives rather than Mary's biological children, while an ancient Eastern Christian tradition identifies them as Joseph's children from an earlier marriage. These interpretations preserve the doctrine of Mary's perpetual virginity.

cards.head: WE DON'T ACTUALLY KNOW
cards.body: The New Testament clearly identifies people as Jesus's brothers and sisters but doesn't explain the precise family relationship in modern terms. What is clear is that at least one of them, James, became enormously important after Jesus's death.

cards.head: WHY THIS DETAIL STAYS AWKWARD
cards.body: The text says one thing and centuries of doctrine say another, and both are still in circulation. Questions that different traditions answer differently do not fade, they get inherited.
